Throughout history, various civilizations have erected colossal statues to honour significant figures and deities. These grand monuments often serve as powerful symbols of cultural pride, religious reverence, and national identity. From ancient times to the modern era, the creation of these massive sculptures has required remarkable feats of engineering and artistry, reflecting the advanced capabilities and artistic vision of their creators.
Today, many of these statues stand as testaments to human ingenuity and cultural heritage.
They represent more than just impressive architectural achievements; they embody the values, beliefs, and historical narratives of the societies that built them. These towering figures, whether of deities, leaders, or historical icons, offer insight into the civilizations that revered them, providing valuable context for understanding the evolution of human culture and art.
In addition to their historical and cultural significance, these monumental statues play a crucial role in boosting tourism. Visitors from around the world are drawn to these awe-inspiring structures, eager to witness the tallest statues in the world. The tourism generated by these sites contributes significantly to local economies, creating jobs and supporting businesses. This influx of visitors also fosters cultural exchange, as people from diverse backgrounds come together to appreciate these shared human achievements.

## List of top tallest statues in the world

## World's tallest statues
### Statue of Unity
Location: Kevadia, Gujarat, India | Height: 182 metres (597 feet) | Completion Date: October 31, 2018
The Statue of Unity, the tallest statue in the world, honours Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, a key figure in India's independence struggle. Designed by Ram V. Sutar, featuring a 153-metre viewing gallery and boosts the local economy.

## World's tallest statues
### Spring Temple Buddha
Location: Lushan County, Henan, China | Height: 128 metres (420 feet) (153 metres including the pedestal) | Completion Date: 2008
The Spring Temple Buddha, the second tallest statue in the world, stands at 153 metres (502 feet) in Fodushan Scenic Area, featuring a temple, monastery, and Buddhist Museum museum, following its completion.

## World's tallest statues
### Laykyun Sekkya
Location: Khatakan Taung, Myanmar | Height: 115.8 metres (380 feet) (129.2 metres including the throne) | Completion Date: 2008
The Laykyun Sekkya statue in Myanmar is the world's third tallest statue, representing Buddha on a 13.5-meter throne. It features an internal structure for visitors to ascend and view Buddhist teachings and iconography.

## World's tallest statues
### Ushiku Daibutsu
Location: Ushiku, Japan | Height: 100m | Completion Date: 1993
Upon its completion in 1993, the statue of Buddha known as Ushiku Daibutsu was the tallest in the world, holding this record for 15 years. Inside the statue, an elevator takes visitors up 85 meters to an observation deck, offering impressive views. It is also believed to be the heaviest statue ever built, weighing over 4,000 tonnes. This bronze statue commemorates the birth of Shinran, a significant Japanese monk who founded the 'Shin' branch of Buddhism, the most widely practiced form of Buddhism in Japan.

## World's tallest statues
### Guishan Guanyin
Location: Hunan, China | Height: 99m | Completion Date: 2009
To reach the Guishan Guanyin of the Thousand Hands and Eyes statue, you must ascend the numerous flights of stairs at Miyin Temple, a Chan Buddhist temple in Weishan, China. At the top, you are rewarded with a gilded bronze monument representing a manifestation of the Bodhisattva Guanyin known as Shiyimian Qianshou Guanyin. The statue was completed in 2009 at a cost of approximately £28 million.

## World's tallest statues
### Mother of All Asia
Location: Pagkilatan, Philippines | Height: 98.15 m | Completion Date: 2021
The 'Mother of All Asia' statue is the world's tallest depiction of the Virgin Mary, symbolizing peace and unity. Located at the Montemaria International Pilgrimage & Conference Center in Batangas City, Philippines, it was completed in 2021. Though relatively simple compared to some other statues, it is nonetheless impressive. Inside, it houses chapels, theatres, shops, food halls, residential spaces, and a shrine to Pope John Paul II.

## World's tallest statues
### Great Buddha of Thailand
Location: Ang Thong, Thailand | Height: 92m | Completion Date: 2008
Located in the Wat Muang Monastery in Ang Thong province, The Great Buddha of Thailand, also known as The Big Buddha or Mahaminh Sakayamunee Visejchaicharn, is one of the largest Buddha statues in Thailand. Photo by Getty Images. Not only is the Great Buddha of Thailand (officially named 'Phra Phuttha Mahanawamintra Sakayamunee Sri Visejchaicharn') impressively tall, but it is also remarkably wide at 63 meters. The statue took 18 years to construct, with building work completed in 2008. Although it appears ostentatious, the statue is made of concrete and painted gold. It was funded by donations from local Buddhists, who raised the £2.2 million needed for its construction.

## World's tallest statues
### Sendai Dai Kannon
Location: Sendai, Japan | Height: 92m | Completion Date: 1991
Next on our list is another impressive statue depicting Dai Kannon. Built in the city of Sendai in 1991, this statue briefly held the title of the world's tallest. Dai Kannon holds the Cintamani Stone, a wish-fulfilling jewel revered in both Buddhism and Hinduism.

## World's tallest statues
### Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park
Location: Ashibetsu, Japan | Height: 88m | Completion Date: 1989
Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park is a statue dedicated to Guanyin, the goddess revered in Buddhism for mercy and compassion. In traditional Chinese Buddhism, Guanyin is depicted as masculine. However, in Japanese culture, the deity is seen as female, reflected in artworks and sculptures. Completed in 1989, construction on the statue concluded when it held the title of the world's tallest until 1991. This statue is one of several erected across Japan during the financial boom of the 1980s by affluent donors. Many of these statues have since deteriorated, and some have been demolished.

The tallest statues in the world
Updated November 3, 2026
Illustration: Quartz
Stand at the base of a colossus, and its size registers in your neck before it registers in your head. The face hovers above the rooftops, and the people milling around its feet look like toys. Societies have raised enormous figures for centuries to declare ambition in a form no one can miss. Each one asks a passerby to look up, and each one prompts a question about the people who built it. What did those builders value enough to cast at this scale? Culture, faith, and collective self-image supply most of the answers, and the biggest of these works turn those abstractions into objects you can walk around.
Height alone gives a misleading picture of these giants. A tape measure can settle which one wins the contest, but it cannot explain what moved anyone to erect it. Some pay tribute to a historical leader. Others embody spiritual devotion. A third group carries a message about unity or national identity, a public argument about who a populace believes it is. Proportion poses its own trap. A photo of a single sculpture against open sky can make a modest piece and a towering one look alike. Nearby pedestrians or buildings give the eye something to compare against, and without those reference points the raw numbers lose their meaning.
HowStuffWorks gathered 15 of the world's tallest statues in a December 2024 list by writer Mack Hayden. The roundup spans 10 countries. China supplies four entries and Japan three, and India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia, the Philippines, Poland, Brazil, and Bhutan contribute one apiece. Each entry pairs a location with feet-and-meters dimensions, plus a brief sketch of what the statue stands for. The publication does not explain how it arrived at those dimensions. Its numbering departs from a clean tallest-to-shortest sequence in several places. The slides that follow keep the publication's order and make no claim about which entry outranks its neighbor in stature. Hayden presents the monuments both as landmarks and as doorways into history and into the ways communities have celebrated their heroes and ideals.

## Statue of Unity honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Illustration: Quartz
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, stands 597 feet, or 182 meters, tall. No other figure on the list reaches that elevation, and HowStuffWorks calls it the reigning champion among the world's tallest statues.
A statesman inspired the giant. The monument honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as India's first deputy prime minister. Its subject sets it apart from most of the company it keeps. Eleven of the 15 entries carry the name of a Buddha, Guan Yin, Kannon, the Virgin Mary, or Christ. The Gujarat monument belongs to a smaller group of four that honors a statesman, a pair of emperors, a legendary general, and a wartime battle.
Patel's likeness outstrips the rest of that group by a wide margin. Emperors Yan and Huang, the tallest of the other three, falls 249 feet short of the Indian figure. The shortfall exceeds the full height of four entries on the list, among them Christ the King and Buddha Dordenma.
Patel's office marks a difference in kind as well. The other three nonreligious entries draw on rulers, legend, and a World War II battle. The Gujarat colossus celebrates a man who held a post in India's own government, a leader from the country's modern political life.
The monument's name points the same direction. Its title holds up unity, a civic ideal, and attaching that word to the tallest entry places a national value at the summit of a list crowded with holy figures.
The Statue of Liberty supplies a familiar yardstick. The Gujarat giant climbs to more than twice the American landmark's stature. Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer offers a second measure, and the Indian statue rises close to five times as high. Both comparisons turn an abstract number into something a reader can picture.
On the list's own figures, no religious statue matches the scale of this tribute to a political leader.

## Spring Temple Buddha reigned for more than a decade
Illustration: Quartz
The Spring Temple Buddha rises 420 feet, or 128 meters, over Lushan County in China, making it the second-tallest statue in the world.
The Chinese figure held the global height record for more than a decade, a run that began before 2008. India's Statue of Unity ended the reign in 2018 and shifted the title to a new country.
A difference of 177 feet, or 54 meters, now separates the two monuments. The Buddha would have to grow by about 42% to recover the crown. The margin exceeds the full height of three entries on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer.
Only two statues in the roundup clear 400 feet, the Statue of Unity and the Spring Temple Buddha itself. Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan comes closest to joining them at 394 feet, 26 feet short of the Lushan County figure. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, the next-tallest Chinese work, stands at 354 feet, 66 feet below the Spring Temple Buddha.
The two gaps point in opposite directions. The Buddha's edge over Japan's tallest statue amounts to a small fraction of its deficit to the Statue of Unity. By height, the Lushan County Buddha sits far closer to the pack below it than to the champion above it. Among the 14 statues trailing the Statue of Unity, only the Spring Temple Buddha comes within 200 feet of it.
The Spring Temple Buddha also stands as the tallest religious figure in the roundup. The Statue of Unity commemorates a political leader. Among monuments to faith, the Lushan County Buddha still holds the height advantage on this list. Losing the overall title in 2018 left its standing among sacred works untouched.

## Laykyun Sekkya Buddha towers over Muang Monastery
Illustration: Quartz
The Laykyun Sekkya Buddha rises 380 feet, or 116 meters, in Monywa, Myanmar, and dwarfs the Muang Monastery below it. The figure portrays the Buddha.
The Myanmar Buddha trails China's Spring Temple Buddha by 40 feet and India's Statue of Unity by 217 feet. It reaches more than three times the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Set against those benchmarks, the Monywa sculpture belongs with the giants at the head of the list. Its deficit against the Spring Temple Buddha amounts to a small slice of its lead over the Brazilian landmark.
Smaller monuments ring the central statue across the grounds. The ring of lesser structures centers the whole site on a single dominant presence. Every one of them sits in the shadow of the main work and underlines its bulk.
A viewing gallery lets visitors approach for a closer look at the Buddha. The gallery gives the statue a second audience, people who study its details in person alongside those who take it in as a silhouette above the monastery. Each feature the list records at Monywa serves the central Buddha, either by framing it from the ground or by drawing viewers toward it.

## Ushiku Daibutsu houses a hall on Buddhism
Illustration: Quartz
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki, Japan, rises 394 feet, or 120 meters, and visitors can walk through rooms inside its body. The statue also goes by the Great Buddha of Ushiku, and the list casts it as a forceful symbol of Japanese culture.
An exhibition hall within the figure teaches guests about Buddhism. The monument doubles as a classroom, and a trip there means studying the faith from inside the Buddha's own likeness.
An observation deck on the top floor opens wide views across the surrounding area. A visitor who moves up from the hall below ends at the sculpture's summit and surveys the landscape from it. The layout makes the Daibutsu a building as well as an artwork, and its height becomes a vantage point that sightseers can occupy.
Its 394 feet put the Great Buddha of Ushiku 14 feet above Myanmar's 380-foot Laykyun Sekkya Buddha. China's Spring Temple Buddha exceeds it by 26 feet, and India's Statue of Unity climbs 203 feet higher. The gap to the Chinese Buddha comes to about one-eighth of the gap to the Indian colossus. The 203-foot shortfall alone surpasses the full stature of several entries, among them Poland's Christ the King and Brazil's Christ the Redeemer.
The Ibaraki Buddha also outstrips its two compatriots in the roundup. It clears Sendai Daikannon's 328 feet by 66 feet and the 289-foot Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park by 105 feet. Its margin over Dai Kannon spans several times the distance separating it from the Spring Temple Buddha. Measured in feet, Japan's largest representative has more in common with the Lushan County giant than with either domestic counterpart.

Humanity has long attempted to create ever-larger statues to express reverence for figures both human and divine, and new giants continue to rise from the foundations of human imagination and ingenuity. Some examples of ancient colossi no longer exist, such as the Colossus of Rhodes (c.294–282 bce), which is estimated to have been about 105 feet (32 meters) tall before it was destroyed in an earthquake about 225/226 bce. With improved construction and architectural techniques, modern statues can scrape the sky and withstand the elements for centuries. The following list presents the ten tallest figurative freestanding statues in the world according to their heights, excluding base-structure height and topographical elevation. The tallest statue today is the Statue of Unity in India, towering 597 feet (182 meters), and the remaining nine are all taller than 275 feet (85 meters). Except for one, all of the 10 tallest statues in the world are found in eastern and southern Asia. Two of the ten tallest statues depict political figures, while the remaining eight represent religious figures: one from Hinduism and seven from Buddhism.

## 1. Statue of Unity
Statue of UnityIndian Air Force helicopters showering rose petals on the Statue of Unity—the world's tallest statue dedicated to Indian independence leader Vallabhbhai Patel—at its inauguration, October 31, 2018. The statue stands at 597 feet (182 meters), or 787 feet (240 meters) with the base, in the Narmada River valley, Gujarat, India.
The tallest statue in the world is the Statue of Unity, a statue of Vallabhbhai Patel that stands 597 feet (182 meters) tall and is located in the state ofGujarat,India. Including the base, it reaches 787 feet (240 meters) high. Vallabhbhai Patel was a leader of the Indian Independence Movement and worked assiduously for the unification of India during its journey toward independence from British colonial rule. He was known as the “Iron Man of India,” and the statue is partially constructed of iron from recycled tools collected from farmers across India. The Statue of Unity is located on a small island in theNarmada River near Ekta Nagar, or Unity Town (previously known as Kevadia). It was inaugurated on October 31, 2018, Patel’s 143rd birth anniversary, at which time it became the world’s tallest statue.

## 2. Spring Temple Buddha
Spring Temple BuddhaA colossal statue of Vairochana Buddha, completed in 2008, standing 420 feet (128 meters) tall at the Foquan Temple, Zhaocun, Lushan county, Henan, China.
Before the Statue of Unity was constructed in India, the title of world’s tallest statue was held by the Spring Temple Buddha, located in Zhaocun, Lushan county, Henan province, China. The statue itself is 420 feet (128 meters) tall, and including the lotus pedestal it reaches a height of 502 feet (153 meters). The colossal Buddha—built of steel, copper alloy, and gold—was constructed between 1997 and 2008. The figure depicted is Vairochana Buddha. In Mahayana and Tibetan Buddhism, there are more buddhas than just the single historical Buddha (Gautama or Shakyamuni Buddha), and Vairochana is considered to be the supreme and cosmic form of the Buddha, of which the others are emanations. The left hand pointing down, palm out, displays the _varadamudra_ (giving gesture, a kind of mudra). The right hand, raised with thumb and middle finger touching, is a form of the _vitarkamudra_ (teaching gesture), which can indicate compassion.
Stone-faced BuddhaThe Leshan Giant Buddha, at 233 feet (71 meters) tall, is the tallest stone Buddha, constructed 713–803, Leshan, Sichuan province, China.
The Buddha has long been a prominent figure depicted in tall statues, and even now Buddha statues comprise half the present list of top ten tallest statues. The Leshan Giant Buddha, built in the 8th century, is 233 feet (71 meters) tall and is the tallest stone Buddha statue. The two Bamiyan Buddha statues in Afghanistan, also made of stone, were created about the 6th century ce and towered 180 feet (55 meters) and 125 feet (38 meters) high, but were destroyed by the Taliban in 2001.

## 3. Laykyun Sekkya
Laykyun SekkyaA reclining colossal Buddha resting in front of a standing Buddha rising 381 feet (116 meters) atop an additional pedestal of 44 feet (13.5 meters) at the Aung Sakkya Pagoda in Khatakan Tuang, Myanmar. Like the Spring Temple Buddha, these Buddhas were also completed in 2008.
A colossal statue of the Buddha located in Myanmar is part of a complex that includes one upright and one reclining statue of the Buddha. The tallest Buddha statue stands 381 feet (116 meters) and is perched atop a pedestal of 44 feet (13.5 meters). In front of the taller statue is another giant statue depicting the Buddha reclining, which portrays the Buddha’s physical death (_parinirvana_). The two statues are cloaked in robes of gold, and they face the Aung Sakkya Pagoda in Khatakan Taung near Monywa, Myanmar. They were completed in 2008 after 12 years of construction.

## 4. Vishwas Swaroopam
Vishwas SwaroopamA colossal statue of the Hindu god Shiva sitting 369 feet (112 meters) tall in Nathdwara, Rajasthan, India.
A tall statue of Shiva, one of the most prominent of the Hindu gods, stands 369 feet (112 meters) tall in the town of Nathdwara in Rajasthan, India. Some sources, however, give a height of 348 feet (106 meters). It is called Vishwas Swaroopam, a Sanskrit-derived name meaning the Statue of Belief. The statue of Shiva was completed in 2022 after 10 years of construction. It is finished with copper that gives the god a reddish-orange hue, and it depicts him seated on a pedestal of 111 feet (34 meters) while holding a _trishul_ (trident). The tallest statues in the world
Updated November 3, 2026
Illustration: Quartz
Stand at the base of a colossus, and its size registers in your neck before it registers in your head. The face hovers above the rooftops, and the people milling around its feet look like toys. Societies have raised enormous figures for centuries to declare ambition in a form no one can miss. Each one asks a passerby to look up, and each one prompts a question about the people who built it. What did those builders value enough to cast at this scale? Culture, faith, and collective self-image supply most of the answers, and the biggest of these works turn those abstractions into objects you can walk around.
Height alone gives a misleading picture of these giants. A tape measure can settle which one wins the contest, but it cannot explain what moved anyone to erect it. Some pay tribute to a historical leader. Others embody spiritual devotion. A third group carries a message about unity or national identity, a public argument about who a populace believes it is. Proportion poses its own trap. A photo of a single sculpture against open sky can make a modest piece and a towering one look alike. Nearby pedestrians or buildings give the eye something to compare against, and without those reference points the raw numbers lose their meaning.
HowStuffWorks gathered 15 of the world's tallest statues in a December 2024 list by writer Mack Hayden. The roundup spans 10 countries. China supplies four entries and Japan three, and India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia, the Philippines, Poland, Brazil, and Bhutan contribute one apiece. Each entry pairs a location with feet-and-meters dimensions, plus a brief sketch of what the statue stands for. The publication does not explain how it arrived at those dimensions. Its numbering departs from a clean tallest-to-shortest sequence in several places. The slides that follow keep the publication's order and make no claim about which entry outranks its neighbor in stature. Hayden presents the monuments both as landmarks and as doorways into history and into the ways communities have celebrated their heroes and ideals.

## Statue of Unity honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Illustration: Quartz
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, stands 597 feet, or 182 meters, tall. No other figure on the list reaches that elevation, and HowStuffWorks calls it the reigning champion among the world's tallest statues.
A statesman inspired the giant. The monument honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as India's first deputy prime minister. Its subject sets it apart from most of the company it keeps. Eleven of the 15 entries carry the name of a Buddha, Guan Yin, Kannon, the Virgin Mary, or Christ. The Gujarat monument belongs to a smaller group of four that honors a statesman, a pair of emperors, a legendary general, and a wartime battle.
Patel's likeness outstrips the rest of that group by a wide margin. Emperors Yan and Huang, the tallest of the other three, falls 249 feet short of the Indian figure. The shortfall exceeds the full height of four entries on the list, among them Christ the King and Buddha Dordenma.
Patel's office marks a difference in kind as well. The other three nonreligious entries draw on rulers, legend, and a World War II battle. The Gujarat colossus celebrates a man who held a post in India's own government, a leader from the country's modern political life.
The monument's name points the same direction. Its title holds up unity, a civic ideal, and attaching that word to the tallest entry places a national value at the summit of a list crowded with holy figures.
The Statue of Liberty supplies a familiar yardstick. The Gujarat giant climbs to more than twice the American landmark's stature. Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer offers a second measure, and the Indian statue rises close to five times as high. Both comparisons turn an abstract number into something a reader can picture.
On the list's own figures, no religious statue matches the scale of this tribute to a political leader.

## Spring Temple Buddha reigned for more than a decade
Illustration: Quartz
The Spring Temple Buddha rises 420 feet, or 128 meters, over Lushan County in China, making it the second-tallest statue in the world.
The Chinese figure held the global height record for more than a decade, a run that began before 2008. India's Statue of Unity ended the reign in 2018 and shifted the title to a new country.
A difference of 177 feet, or 54 meters, now separates the two monuments. The Buddha would have to grow by about 42% to recover the crown. The margin exceeds the full height of three entries on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer.
Only two statues in the roundup clear 400 feet, the Statue of Unity and the Spring Temple Buddha itself. Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan comes closest to joining them at 394 feet, 26 feet short of the Lushan County figure. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, the next-tallest Chinese work, stands at 354 feet, 66 feet below the Spring Temple Buddha.
The two gaps point in opposite directions. The Buddha's edge over Japan's tallest statue amounts to a small fraction of its deficit to the Statue of Unity. By height, the Lushan County Buddha sits far closer to the pack below it than to the champion above it. Among the 14 statues trailing the Statue of Unity, only the Spring Temple Buddha comes within 200 feet of it.
The Spring Temple Buddha also stands as the tallest religious figure in the roundup. The Statue of Unity commemorates a political leader. Among monuments to faith, the Lushan County Buddha still holds the height advantage on this list. Losing the overall title in 2018 left its standing among sacred works untouched.

## Laykyun Sekkya Buddha towers over Muang Monastery
Illustration: Quartz
The Laykyun Sekkya Buddha rises 380 feet, or 116 meters, in Monywa, Myanmar, and dwarfs the Muang Monastery below it. The figure portrays the Buddha.
The Myanmar Buddha trails China's Spring Temple Buddha by 40 feet and India's Statue of Unity by 217 feet. It reaches more than three times the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Set against those benchmarks, the Monywa sculpture belongs with the giants at the head of the list. Its deficit against the Spring Temple Buddha amounts to a small slice of its lead over the Brazilian landmark.
Smaller monuments ring the central statue across the grounds. The ring of lesser structures centers the whole site on a single dominant presence. Every one of them sits in the shadow of the main work and underlines its bulk.
A viewing gallery lets visitors approach for a closer look at the Buddha. The gallery gives the statue a second audience, people who study its details in person alongside those who take it in as a silhouette above the monastery. Each feature the list records at Monywa serves the central Buddha, either by framing it from the ground or by drawing viewers toward it.
texts.4:
## Ushiku Daibutsu houses a hall on Buddhism
Illustration: Quartz
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki, Japan, rises 394 feet, or 120 meters, and visitors can walk through rooms inside its body. The statue also goes by the Great Buddha of Ushiku, and the list casts it as a forceful symbol of Japanese culture.
An exhibition hall within the figure teaches guests about Buddhism. The monument doubles as a classroom, and a trip there means studying the faith from inside the Buddha's own likeness.
An observation deck on the top floor opens wide views across the surrounding area. A visitor who moves up from the hall below ends at the sculpture's summit and surveys the landscape from it. The layout makes the Daibutsu a building as well as an artwork, and its height becomes a vantage point that sightseers can occupy.
Its 394 feet put the Great Buddha of Ushiku 14 feet above Myanmar's 380-foot Laykyun Sekkya Buddha. China's Spring Temple Buddha exceeds it by 26 feet, and India's Statue of Unity climbs 203 feet higher. The gap to the Chinese Buddha comes to about one-eighth of the gap to the Indian colossus. The 203-foot shortfall alone surpasses the full stature of several entries, among them Poland's Christ the King and Brazil's Christ the Redeemer.
The Ibaraki Buddha also outstrips its two compatriots in the roundup. It clears Sendai Daikannon's 328 feet by 66 feet and the 289-foot Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park by 105 feet. Its margin over Dai Kannon spans several times the distance separating it from the Spring Temple Buddha. Measured in feet, Japan's largest representative has more in common with the Lushan County giant than with either domestic counterpart.

Some examples of ancient colossi no longer exist, such as the Colossus of Rhodes (c.294–282 bce), which is estimated to have been about 105 feet (32 meters) tall before it was destroyed in an earthquake about 225/226 bce. With improved construction and architectural techniques, modern statues can scrape the sky and withstand the elements for centuries. The following list presents the ten tallest figurative freestanding statues in the world according to their heights, excluding base-structure height and topographical elevation. The tallest statue today is the Statue of Unity in India, towering 597 feet (182 meters), and the remaining nine are all taller than 275 feet (85 meters). The tallest statues in the world
Updated November 3, 2026
Illustration: Quartz
Stand at the base of a colossus, and its size registers in your neck before it registers in your head. The face hovers above the rooftops, and the people milling around its feet look like toys. Societies have raised enormous figures for centuries to declare ambition in a form no one can miss. Each one asks a passerby to look up, and each one prompts a question about the people who built it. What did those builders value enough to cast at this scale? Culture, faith, and collective self-image supply most of the answers, and the biggest of these works turn those abstractions into objects you can walk around.
Height alone gives a misleading picture of these giants. A tape measure can settle which one wins the contest, but it cannot explain what moved anyone to erect it. Some pay tribute to a historical leader. Others embody spiritual devotion. A third group carries a message about unity or national identity, a public argument about who a populace believes it is. Proportion poses its own trap. A photo of a single sculpture against open sky can make a modest piece and a towering one look alike. Nearby pedestrians or buildings give the eye something to compare against, and without those reference points the raw numbers lose their meaning.
HowStuffWorks gathered 15 of the world's tallest statues in a December 2024 list by writer Mack Hayden. The roundup spans 10 countries. China supplies four entries and Japan three, and India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia, the Philippines, Poland, Brazil, and Bhutan contribute one apiece. Each entry pairs a location with feet-and-meters dimensions, plus a brief sketch of what the statue stands for. The publication does not explain how it arrived at those dimensions. Its numbering departs from a clean tallest-to-shortest sequence in several places. The slides that follow keep the publication's order and make no claim about which entry outranks its neighbor in stature. Hayden presents the monuments both as landmarks and as doorways into history and into the ways communities have celebrated their heroes and ideals.

## Statue of Unity honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Illustration: Quartz
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, stands 597 feet, or 182 meters, tall. No other figure on the list reaches that elevation, and HowStuffWorks calls it the reigning champion among the world's tallest statues.
A statesman inspired the giant. The monument honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as India's first deputy prime minister. Its subject sets it apart from most of the company it keeps. Eleven of the 15 entries carry the name of a Buddha, Guan Yin, Kannon, the Virgin Mary, or Christ. The Gujarat monument belongs to a smaller group of four that honors a statesman, a pair of emperors, a legendary general, and a wartime battle.
Patel's likeness outstrips the rest of that group by a wide margin. Emperors Yan and Huang, the tallest of the other three, falls 249 feet short of the Indian figure. The shortfall exceeds the full height of four entries on the list, among them Christ the King and Buddha Dordenma.
Patel's office marks a difference in kind as well. The other three nonreligious entries draw on rulers, legend, and a World War II battle. The Gujarat colossus celebrates a man who held a post in India's own government, a leader from the country's modern political life.
The monument's name points the same direction. Its title holds up unity, a civic ideal, and attaching that word to the tallest entry places a national value at the summit of a list crowded with holy figures.
The Statue of Liberty supplies a familiar yardstick. The Gujarat giant climbs to more than twice the American landmark's stature. Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer offers a second measure, and the Indian statue rises close to five times as high. Both comparisons turn an abstract number into something a reader can picture.
On the list's own figures, no religious statue matches the scale of this tribute to a political leader.

## Spring Temple Buddha reigned for more than a decade
Illustration: Quartz
The Spring Temple Buddha rises 420 feet, or 128 meters, over Lushan County in China, making it the second-tallest statue in the world.
The Chinese figure held the global height record for more than a decade, a run that began before 2008. India's Statue of Unity ended the reign in 2018 and shifted the title to a new country.
A difference of 177 feet, or 54 meters, now separates the two monuments. The Buddha would have to grow by about 42% to recover the crown. The margin exceeds the full height of three entries on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer.
Only two statues in the roundup clear 400 feet, the Statue of Unity and the Spring Temple Buddha itself. Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan comes closest to joining them at 394 feet, 26 feet short of the Lushan County figure. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, the next-tallest Chinese work, stands at 354 feet, 66 feet below the Spring Temple Buddha.
The two gaps point in opposite directions. The Buddha's edge over Japan's tallest statue amounts to a small fraction of its deficit to the Statue of Unity. By height, the Lushan County Buddha sits far closer to the pack below it than to the champion above it. Among the 14 statues trailing the Statue of Unity, only the Spring Temple Buddha comes within 200 feet of it.
The Spring Temple Buddha also stands as the tallest religious figure in the roundup. The Statue of Unity commemorates a political leader. Among monuments to faith, the Lushan County Buddha still holds the height advantage on this list. Losing the overall title in 2018 left its standing among sacred works untouched.

## Laykyun Sekkya Buddha towers over Muang Monastery
Illustration: Quartz
The Laykyun Sekkya Buddha rises 380 feet, or 116 meters, in Monywa, Myanmar, and dwarfs the Muang Monastery below it. The figure portrays the Buddha.
The Myanmar Buddha trails China's Spring Temple Buddha by 40 feet and India's Statue of Unity by 217 feet. It reaches more than three times the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Set against those benchmarks, the Monywa sculpture belongs with the giants at the head of the list. Its deficit against the Spring Temple Buddha amounts to a small slice of its lead over the Brazilian landmark.
Smaller monuments ring the central statue across the grounds. The ring of lesser structures centers the whole site on a single dominant presence. Every one of them sits in the shadow of the main work and underlines its bulk.
A viewing gallery lets visitors approach for a closer look at the Buddha. The gallery gives the statue a second audience, people who study its details in person alongside those who take it in as a silhouette above the monastery. Each feature the list records at Monywa serves the central Buddha, either by framing it from the ground or by drawing viewers toward it.

## Ushiku Daibutsu houses a hall on Buddhism
Illustration: Quartz
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki, Japan, rises 394 feet, or 120 meters, and visitors can walk through rooms inside its body. The statue also goes by the Great Buddha of Ushiku, and the list casts it as a forceful symbol of Japanese culture.
An exhibition hall within the figure teaches guests about Buddhism. The monument doubles as a classroom, and a trip there means studying the faith from inside the Buddha's own likeness.
An observation deck on the top floor opens wide views across the surrounding area. A visitor who moves up from the hall below ends at the sculpture's summit and surveys the landscape from it. The layout makes the Daibutsu a building as well as an artwork, and its height becomes a vantage point that sightseers can occupy.
Its 394 feet put the Great Buddha of Ushiku 14 feet above Myanmar's 380-foot Laykyun Sekkya Buddha. China's Spring Temple Buddha exceeds it by 26 feet, and India's Statue of Unity climbs 203 feet higher. The gap to the Chinese Buddha comes to about one-eighth of the gap to the Indian colossus. The 203-foot shortfall alone surpasses the full stature of several entries, among them Poland's Christ the King and Brazil's Christ the Redeemer.
The Ibaraki Buddha also outstrips its two compatriots in the roundup. It clears Sendai Daikannon's 328 feet by 66 feet and the 289-foot Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park by 105 feet. Its margin over Dai Kannon spans several times the distance separating it from the Spring Temple Buddha. Measured in feet, Japan's largest representative has more in common with the Lushan County giant than with either domestic counterpart.

Humanity has long attempted to create ever-larger statues to express reverence for figures both human and divine, and new giants continue to rise from the foundations of human imagination and ingenuity. Some examples of ancient colossi no longer exist, such as the Colossus of Rhodes (c.294–282 bce), which is estimated to have been about 105 feet (32 meters) tall before it was destroyed in an earthquake about 225/226 bce. With improved construction and architectural techniques, modern statues can scrape the sky and withstand the elements for centuries. The following list presents the ten tallest figurative freestanding statues in the world according to their heights, excluding base-structure height and topographical elevation. The tallest statue today is the Statue of Unity in India, towering 597 feet (182 meters), and the remaining nine are all taller than 275 feet (85 meters). Except for one, all of the 10 tallest statues in the world are found in eastern and southern Asia. Two of the ten tallest statues depict political figures, while the remaining eight represent religious figures: one from Hinduism and seven from Buddhism.

## 1. Statue of Unity
Statue of UnityIndian Air Force helicopters showering rose petals on the Statue of Unity—the world's tallest statue dedicated to Indian independence leader Vallabhbhai Patel—at its inauguration, October 31, 2018. The statue stands at 597 feet (182 meters), or 787 feet (240 meters) with the base, in the Narmada River valley, Gujarat, India.
The tallest statue in the world is the Statue of Unity, a statue of Vallabhbhai Patel that stands 597 feet (182 meters) tall and is located in the state ofGujarat,India. Including the base, it reaches 787 feet (240 meters) high. Vallabhbhai Patel was a leader of the Indian Independence Movement and worked assiduously for the unification of India during its journey toward independence from British colonial rule. He was known as the “Iron Man of India,” and the statue is partially constructed of iron from recycled tools collected from farmers across India. The Statue of Unity is located on a small island in theNarmada River near Ekta Nagar, or Unity Town (previously known as Kevadia). It was inaugurated on October 31, 2018, Patel’s 143rd birth anniversary, at which time it became the world’s tallest statue.

## 2. Spring Temple Buddha
Spring Temple BuddhaA colossal statue of Vairochana Buddha, completed in 2008, standing 420 feet (128 meters) tall at the Foquan Temple, Zhaocun, Lushan county, Henan, China.
Before the Statue of Unity was constructed in India, the title of world’s tallest statue was held by the Spring Temple Buddha, located in Zhaocun, Lushan county, Henan province, China. The statue itself is 420 feet (128 meters) tall, and including the lotus pedestal it reaches a height of 502 feet (153 meters). The colossal Buddha—built of steel, copper alloy, and gold—was constructed between 1997 and 2008. The figure depicted is Vairochana Buddha. In Mahayana and Tibetan Buddhism, there are more buddhas than just the single historical Buddha (Gautama or Shakyamuni Buddha), and Vairochana is considered to be the supreme and cosmic form of the Buddha, of which the others are emanations. The left hand pointing down, palm out, displays the _varadamudra_ (giving gesture, a kind of mudra). The right hand, raised with thumb and middle finger touching, is a form of the _vitarkamudra_ (teaching gesture), which can indicate compassion.
Stone-faced BuddhaThe Leshan Giant Buddha, at 233 feet (71 meters) tall, is the tallest stone Buddha, constructed 713–803, Leshan, Sichuan province, China.
The Buddha has long been a prominent figure depicted in tall statues, and even now Buddha statues comprise half the present list of top ten tallest statues. The Leshan Giant Buddha, built in the 8th century, is 233 feet (71 meters) tall and is the tallest stone Buddha statue. The two Bamiyan Buddha statues in Afghanistan, also made of stone, were created about the 6th century ce and towered 180 feet (55 meters) and 125 feet (38 meters) high, but were destroyed by the Taliban in 2001.

## 3. Laykyun Sekkya
Laykyun SekkyaA reclining colossal Buddha resting in front of a standing Buddha rising 381 feet (116 meters) atop an additional pedestal of 44 feet (13.5 meters) at the Aung Sakkya Pagoda in Khatakan Tuang, Myanmar. Like the Spring Temple Buddha, these Buddhas were also completed in 2008.
A colossal statue of the Buddha located in Myanmar is part of a complex that includes one upright and one reclining statue of the Buddha. The tallest Buddha statue stands 381 feet (116 meters) and is perched atop a pedestal of 44 feet (13.5 meters). In front of the taller statue is another giant statue depicting the Buddha reclining, which portrays the Buddha’s physical death (_parinirvana_). The two statues are cloaked in robes of gold, and they face the Aung Sakkya Pagoda in Khatakan Taung near Monywa, Myanmar. They were completed in 2008 after 12 years of construction.

## 4. Vishwas Swaroopam
Vishwas SwaroopamA colossal statue of the Hindu god Shiva sitting 369 feet (112 meters) tall in Nathdwara, Rajasthan, India.
A tall statue of Shiva, one of the most prominent of the Hindu gods, stands 369 feet (112 meters) tall in the town of Nathdwara in Rajasthan, India. Some sources, however, give a height of 348 feet (106 meters). It is called Vishwas Swaroopam, a Sanskrit-derived name meaning the Statue of Belief. The statue of Shiva was completed in 2022 after 10 years of construction. It is finished with copper that gives the god a reddish-orange hue, and it depicts him seated on a pedestal of 111 feet (34 meters) while holding a _trishul_ (trident). The fact that he is seated on a pedestal that is nearly one-third the total height, with only his right foot reaching toward the ground, raises a question about whether the statue can be considered fully freestanding.

## 5. Ushiku Daibutsu
Ushiku DaibutsuA bronze statue of Amida Buddha, a savior figure in Pure Land Buddhism standing 330 feet (100 meters) tall, excluding the pedestal in Ushiku City, Ibaraki prefecture, Japan.
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan rises 330 feet (100 meters) in Ushiku City,Ibaraki prefecture. Made of bronze, it stands atop a pedestal of 66 feet (20 meters). It was built in 1993. The statue depicts Amida Buddha, the Japanese name for Amitabha Buddha, a savior buddha who is a key figure in Pure Land Buddhism. The statue’s overall 120-meter height is a reference to the 12 rays of light of Amida Buddha according to Pure Land Buddhism. In addition to an observation deck at 278 feet (85 meters), the construction includes rooms for Buddhist meditation and calligraphy and a collection of Buddhist relics.
